newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico grants Repsol natgas rights.
newsitem.headline: Mexico grants Repsol natgas rights.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Thursday it awarded Repsol's Mexico unit the rights to natural gas distribution in the region surrounding Saltillo, Coahuila state.

The company has distributed natural gas in the zone since 1960 under a provisional permit, and the CRE said in the Official Gazette that it recently decided to award Repsol the more permanent, 30-year concession.

Rather than the public auction the CRE usually stages for such concessions, it can grant the rights to a company that is seen fit to continue the distribution and has an established presence in the area.

Repsol Mexico SA committed to spend about $39 million on infrastructure development in the first five years of the concession. It agreed to charge a maximum average 25.33 pesos per gigacalorie and service at least 40,027 residents by the fifth year of operations.
The industrial region of Saltillo, Ramos Arizpo and Arteaga has estimated daily consumption of seven billion kilocalories, the CRE has said.
Mexico is privatizing natural gas distribution in an effort to boost use of the fuel and to modernize its transport.
